verses.15:1: {conserva}, Senhor, porque em vós esperei. ‡ Eu disse ao Senhor: Vós sois o meu Deus, * porque {eges}.
verses.15:3: {sanctis} que estão na sua terra, * {mirificavit} todas as minhas vontades neles.
verses.15:5: {calicis}: * sois vós que me restituireis a minha herança.
verses.15:6: As cordas me caíram {praeclaris}: * pois a minha herança é {praeclara} para mim.
verses.15:7: Bendirei o Senhor, que me deu entendimento: * {noctem} me repreenderam.
verses.15:8: {providebam}: * porque está à minha direita, para eu não ser abalado.
verses.15:9: Por isso se alegrou o meu coração, e exultou a minha língua: * e ainda a minha carne repousará na esperança.
verses.15:10: Porque não abandonareis a minha alma {inferno}: * nem {dabis} a corrupção.
verses.15:11: Fizestes-me conhecer os caminhos da vida, † vós me enchereis de alegria com o vosso rosto: * {delectationes} na vossa direita {finem}.

decisions.why: consérvare: 'keep, preserve' (φύλαξόν με). The glossary rules serváre with a person as object → 'conservar' (Ps 11:8 'nos conservareis', beside custodíre → guardar); the Greek there is also φυλάσσω. conserváre is only here and 36:28 in ætérnum conservabúntur (grep). 'Conservai' is safe at the vós imperative (past 'conservei'). Douay-Rheims 'Preserve me'; Matos Soares 1932 'Guarda-me'.

options.label: Conservai-me
options.note: Ruling: the cognate, one family with 11:8's serváre → 'conservar'; the verb of the blessing 'Deus vos conserve'. It leaves 'guardar' to custodíre (16:8a Custódi me).

options.label: Guardai-me
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the familiar opening, but 'guardar' is custodíre's, and 16:8a Custódi me, one psalm later, needs it.

options.label: Preservai-me
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'Preserve'; a third verb for the family.

decisions.why: egére + genitive: 'to need, have need of' (οὐ χρείαν ἔχεις); only here in the psalter (grep). Its adjective egénus is proposed → 'necessitado' (glossary, inops row). The Latin says it because God is God (the Hebrew differs). Douay-Rheims 'for thou hast no need of my goods'; Matos Soares 1932 'Que não tens necessidade dos meus bens'.

options.label: não precisais dos meus bens
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb; the verse closes on the stressed 'bens' as the Latin's colon on 'eges'.

options.label: não tendes necessidade dos meus bens

forms.eges: não tendes necessidade dos meus bens

options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the noun, and a link to 'necessitado' (egénus); three syllables longer.

options.label: não necessitais dos meus bens
options.note: The verb of egénus's proposed family; bookish.

decisions.latin: Sanctis, qui sunt in terra ejus
decisions.why: A dative standing first and hanging loose ('To the saints who are in his land'), taken up by 'in eis' at the end; the Greek has the same (τοῖς ἁγίοις … ἐν αὐτοῖς), though its 'wills' are 'his' (αὐτοῦ) where the Latin has 'meas' — the Latin is followed (rule 1). The verse is famously obscure; the Latin's looseness is kept, not explained. Douay-Rheims 'To the saints, who are in his land'; Matos Soares 1932 'Para com os santos, que estão sobre a sua terra'. Heard (draft 1): the stylist’s worst line — «A abertura fica sintaticamente suspensa; depois da pausa, “fez maravilhosas” soa como uma construção transportada do latim» → ‘Quanto aos santos … tornou maravilhosas’. Refused: the suspension is the Latin’s own (a hanging dative taken up by in eis), and ‘Quanto aos’ decides the grammar the Latin leaves open; his line is option 3. The blind reader heard ‘fez maravilhosas’ with the Lord as subject, as meant; ‘todas as minhas vontades neles’ he found unclear — so is the Latin.

options.label: Aos santos
options.note: Ruling: the dative as Portuguese has it, left hanging as in the Latin and Douay-Rheims.

options.label: Para com os santos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: says 'towards', a relation the Latin does not name.

options.label: Quanto aos santos
options.note: Makes the loose dative a topic ('as for'); an interpretation of the grammar. The stylist’s line.

decisions.latin: mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis
decisions.why: Glossary: mirificáre → fazer maravilhoso (working; 4:4 mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum → 'fez maravilhoso o seu santo' — the same verb beside the same noun, sanctus; the row names 15:3). No subject in the Latin; 'terra ejus' and the psalm make it God. voluntas → vontade (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'he hath made wonderful all my desires in them'; Matos Soares 1932 'fez brilhar todo o meu afecto' (explains).

options.label: fez maravilhosas
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb, agreeing with 'vontades'; no subject supplied, as the Latin (the Lord of 15:2 is heard). The echo of 4:4 (santo … fez maravilhoso) is kept.

options.label: ele fez maravilhosas
options.note: The subject named (D2 allows it); 'ele' is as open as the verb ending.

options.label: fez brilhar
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb (he then drops 'omnes voluntátes meas in eis' for 'todo o meu afecto').

options.label: tornou maravilhosas
options.note: The stylist’s verb. Refused: the glossary’s mirificáre → ‘fazer maravilhoso’ (4:4 ‘fez maravilhoso o seu santo’, the same verb beside the same noun).

decisions.why: acceleráre: 'to hasten' (ἐτάχυναν); only here and 30:3 accélera ut éruas me (grep) — there of God, at the vós imperative ('apressai-vos', safe). eórum (whose infirmities) is left as open as the Latin: 'deles'. Douay-Rheims 'afterwards they made haste'; Matos Soares 1932 'depois correram aceleradamente'.

options.label: se apressaram
options.note: Ruling: one verb for one, plain; 30:3 can have 'apressai-vos'.

options.label: correram depressa
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense; 'correr' supplies a motion the Latin does not name, and 'depressa' is velóciter's.

decisions.latin: Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus
decisions.why: 'I will not gather their gatherings of bloods' (οὐ μὴ συναγάγω τὰς συναγωγὰς αὐτῶν ἐξ αἱμάτων): the Greek repeats one root, the Latin has two of one sense (congregáre / conventículum, L&S 'an assembly, meeting'); only here (grep). sanguínes (plural: bloodshed, blood offerings) → 'de sangue', the plural lost as in the glossary's vir sánguinum → homem de sangue; 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus is the other plural. congregáre (17 lines with the stem) and congregátio (→ congregação, the row synagóga) are one family. Douay-Rheims 'I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings' (explains); Matos Soares 1932 'Não congregarei os seus conventículos sanguinários'. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — «O singular elimina o plural concreto e incomum do latim» → ‘de sangues’. HELD: the glossary row vir sánguinum → ‘homem de sangue’ (5:7b; 25:9, 54:24, 138:19 to follow) already loses the same plural, and one ruling must serve all six places of the plural (with 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus). In Portuguese ‘sangue’ is a mass noun; ‘sangues’ is heard as a slip or as kinds of blood, not as ‘bloodshed’. The blind reader heard ‘de sangue’ as ‘reuniões com derramamento de sangue’ first and ‘ritos com sangue’ second — the two readings of the plural. Proposed to the glossary as an open row for Gustavo (sanguínes, plural).

options.label: congregarei os seus ajuntamentos
options.note: Ruling: 'congregar', the Latin's verb, of one family with congregátio → congregação; 'ajuntamento', a plain word for a gathering that is not the glossary's 'assembleia' (concílium) nor 'congregação'. 'de sangue' left as open as the Latin (blood shed, blood offered).

options.label: congregarei os seus conventículos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's cognate: in Portuguese a secret, factious meeting — apt, but rare and a proparoxytone.

options.label: reunirei as suas reuniões
options.note: The Greek's figure (one root twice); the Latin varies it.

options.label: congregarei os seus ajuntamentos … de sangues
options.note: The Latinist’s fix: the plural kept. Refused (held against a major): the glossary’s vir sánguinum → ‘homem de sangue’ loses the plural, and ‘sangues’ is heard as a slip.

decisions.latin: nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea
decisions.why: 'Nor will I be mindful of their names through my lips' — I will not take their names on my lips (διὰ χειλέων μου). memor esse → lembrar-se de (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'by my lips'; Matos Soares 1932 'nem sequer me lembrarei dos seus nomes para os pronunciar' (explains). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «“Lábios” é proparoxítono e deixa duas sílabas átonas depois do último apoio» → ‘nem pelos meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’. Taken in its order (rule 4), with the ruling’s ‘com’ (the instrument).

options.label: com os meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes

forms.perlabia: com os meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s order — the lips before the verb, so the verse ends on the paroxytone ‘nomes’ (rule 4; the ear leads on order, D28). ‘com’ kept for per (the instrument: to remember aloud, to name).

options.label: me lembrarei dos seus nomes com os meus lábios

forms.perlabia: me lembrarei dos seus nomes com os meus lábios

options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s order; the verse ends on the proparoxytone ‘lábios’.

options.label: pelos meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes

forms.perlabia: pelos meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes

options.note: The stylist’s line: ‘per’ to the letter; ‘pelos’ can be heard as ‘for the sake of’.

options.label: me lembrarei dos seus nomes pelos meus lábios

forms.perlabia: me lembrarei dos seus nomes pelos meus lábios

options.note: 'per' to the letter; 'pelos' can be heard as 'for the sake of'.

decisions.latin: Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei
decisions.why: Glossary: calix / pars → cálice / parte (working; its row names 15:5); heréditas → herança. The Latin has no verb (Portuguese supplies 'é'). 'cálice' is a proparoxytone and here stands at the mediant, which the glossary says wants a word after it (10:7 'do cálice deles'). Douay-Rheims 'The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup'; Matos Soares 1932 'O Senhor é a porção da minha herança e do meu cálice'. Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «“Cálice” é proparoxítono» → ‘A parte da minha herança e do meu cálice é o Senhor: * sois vós que me restituireis a minha herança’. Refused, kept as an option: the Latin opens on Dóminus, and the verse turns from ‘O Senhor’ to ‘sois vós’ — both colons open on the person; his order ends the colon on ‘Senhor’ and moves the turn.

options.label: O Senhor é a parte da minha herança e do meu cálice

forms.calicis: O Senhor é a parte da minha herança e do meu cálice

options.note: Ruling (drafts 1–2): the Latin’s words in the Latin’s order; the proparoxytone at the mediant accepted (as Ps 90:1 ‘Altíssimo’). The stylist’s order refused: it moves Dóminus from the head of the verse.

options.label: O Senhor é a parte da minha herança e do cálice meu

forms.calicis: O Senhor é a parte da minha herança e do cálice meu

options.note: The possessive after: the mediant on a stressed syllable, at the cost of a poetic inversion (rule 5).

options.label: A parte da minha herança e do meu cálice é o Senhor

forms.calicis: A parte da minha herança e do meu cálice é o Senhor

options.note: The stylist’s line: the mediant on ‘Senhor’; Dóminus leaves the head of the verse.

decisions.latin: Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi
decisions.why: The measuring lines of an allotment fell to me 'in very fine [places]' (ἐν τοῖς κρατίστοις); præclárus 'very bright … magnificent, splendid, excellent' (Lewis & Short); said twice, and the repetition is kept. funes → cordas (glossary, working). præclárus recurs only in 22:5 calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est (grep). Douay-Rheims 'in goodly places … goodly'; Matos Soares 1932 'em lugares deliciosos … excelente'.

options.label: excelentes / excelente
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word twice, as the Latin; a paroxytone at both cadences; 'lugares' supplied for the neuter plural (Douay-Rheims' 'places').

options.label: esplêndidos / esplêndida
options.note: Nearer to 'very bright'; proparoxytones at the mediant and in the last colon.

options.label: deliciosos / excelente
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the repetition lost.

decisions.latin: ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei
decisions.why: ínsuper et → 'e ainda' (glossary, which already writes 15:7 and 15:9 so); increpáre → repreender (glossary; the Greek here is ἐπαίδευσαν, 'instructed, chastened', but the Latin reads 'rebuked'); renes → rins (glossary, open — the organ named). usque ad noctem: 'up to the night' (ἕως νυκτός). Douay-Rheims 'even till night'; Matos Soares 1932 'mesmo durante a noite' and 'o meu coração' (a gloss for the reins). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «A sequência “e ainda até” acumula partículas … “ainda” também pode ser ouvido como indicação de duração» → ‘e até a noite os meus rins também me repreenderam’. Refused, kept as an option: ínsuper et → ‘e ainda’ is the glossary’s, and 15:9 opens its last colon with the same two words (ínsuper et caro mea); the stylist’s ‘também’ breaks the pair. The blind reader heard ‘até a noite’ as ‘until night’ first, ‘even at night’ second — both inside usque ad noctem.

options.label: e ainda até a noite os meus rins

forms.noctem: e ainda até a noite os meus rins

options.note: Ruling (drafts 1–2): ínsuper et → ‘e ainda’ (glossary; the same words open 15:9’s last colon), usque ad → ‘até’; the verse ends on the paroxytone ‘repreenderam’.

options.label: e ainda até de noite os meus rins

forms.noctem: e ainda até de noite os meus rins

options.note: ‘even at night’ — Matos Soares 1932’s sense; ‘até’ as ‘even’ rather than ‘until’.

options.label: e até a noite os meus rins também

forms.noctem: e até a noite os meus rins também

options.note: The stylist’s line: fewer particles in a row; ínsuper becomes ‘também’, and the pair with 15:9 (‘e ainda a minha carne’) is lost.

decisions.latin: Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper
decisions.why: pro-vidére: 'to see forwards or before one's self' and 'to foresee' (Lewis & Short); the Greek προωρώμην, 'I saw before me'. Imperfect. in conspéctu meo → 'à minha vista' (glossary's open proposal for in conspéctu, 5:9; 14:4a 'à vista dele'). 15:8–11 is quoted word for word in Acts 2:25–28 (Clementine fetched: consult/bolls-VULG-44-2.json), and Acts 2:31 goes on 'providens locutus est de resurrectione Christi' — Peter's 'foreseeing'. Only here in the psalter (grep). Douay-Rheims 'I set the Lord always in my sight'; Matos Soares 1932 'Eu contemplava sempre o Senhor diante de mim'. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — «Neste contexto, providébam exprime ver diante de si. “Antevia” introduz antecipação temporal … deslocando a imagem da presença constante diante dos olhos» → ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’; the stylist — «“antevia” sugere prever algo futuro» → ‘Eu via sempre o Senhor diante de mim’; the blind reader listed ‘antevia’ as unknown and heard ‘previa que veria o Senhor’ first. Three readers against one word: taken.

options.label: Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista

forms.providebam: Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the Latinist’s fix, the Latin’s order (Dóminum … in conspéctu meo semper). The προ- is carried by ‘à minha vista’ (before me in place), which is the sense the Greek προωρώμην has here; the temporal foresight is Acts 2:31’s reading (providens), not the verb’s in this verse. ‘via … vista’ says the seeing twice, as pro-vidére … conspéctus does.

options.label: Eu antevia o Senhor sempre à minha vista

forms.providebam: Eu antevia o Senhor sempre à minha vista

options.note: Draft 1. 'ante-ver' is pro-vidére part for part, and holds its 'seeing before' — in time, the sense Acts 2:31 draws out, and, with 'à minha vista', in place. The imperfect kept. To be tested: 'antevia' and 'vista' side by side.

options.label: Eu via sempre o Senhor à minha vista

forms.providebam: Eu via sempre o Senhor à minha vista

options.note: The plain verb; the 'pro-' lost, and 'via … vista' says the seeing twice.

options.label: Eu tinha sempre o Senhor diante de mim

forms.providebam: Eu tinha sempre o Senhor diante de mim

options.note: The sense of Douay-Rheims' 'set'; the seeing lost.

options.label: Eu contemplava sempre o Senhor diante de mim

forms.providebam: Eu contemplava sempre o Senhor diante de mim

options.note: Matos Soares 1932: 'contemplar' is contemplári's.

options.label: Eu via sempre o Senhor diante de mim

forms.providebam: Eu via sempre o Senhor diante de mim

options.note: The stylist’s line. ‘diante de mim’ drops conspéctus’s ‘vista’ (glossary, open; 14:4a ‘À vista dele’).

decisions.latin: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno
decisions.why: One of the two hard places of inférnus (D22; glossary row inférnus / ínferi, open, 'for Gustavo's ear'). inférnus is the underworld, the place of the dead (ᾅδης). Ps 6:6 and 9:18 have 'inferno'. The verse is quoted word for word in Acts 2:27, applied in 2:31 to Christ ('neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro ejus vidit corruptionem') and in Acts 13:35 ('Non dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem') — Clementine text fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-44-2.json and -44-13.json. The Portuguese singular 'inferno' is first heard as the hell of the damned (Ps 6's blind reader). derelínquere → abandonar (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'hell'; Matos Soares 1932 here 'não deixarás a minha alma no inferno' (he paraphrased at 6:6, not here). Heard (draft 1): the blind reader, as feared — ‘no inferno’ first as «o lugar de castigo após a morte», second as «o domínio dos mortos». The Latinist passed it; no critic asked for a change. Kept, for Gustavo’s ear (glossary row inférnus).

options.label: no inferno
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word, as 6:6 and 9:18 have it, as Douay-Rheims and — here — Matos Soares 1932 have it, and as the Vulgate of Acts 2:27, 31 has it in the same words. The hearing of the damned is the risk, and the blind reader is asked; whatever it costs, it is the Latin's own word, and the verse promises that the soul will not be left there.

options.label: nos infernos
options.note: The old plural for the abode of the dead (the Creed's 'desceu aos infernos', from memory, unverified); marks the place of the dead apart from the hell of the damned, at the cost of a number the Latin does not have.

options.label: na mansão dos mortos
options.note: The phrase of the Creed as now said in Brazil (from memory, unverified): the sense, but a paraphrase (rule 2).

options.label: na morada dos mortos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's way at 6:6 ('habitação dos mortos'): a paraphrase.

decisions.latin: nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem
decisions.why: 'dare' + infinitive: 'nor will you give your holy one to see corruption' (οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν) — the Greek and Latin idiom for 'allow'. sanctus (ὅσιος) → santo (glossary), lowercase. corrúptio: decay (διαφθορά); the other place is 29:10 dum descéndo in corruptiónem (grep). Acts 2:27, 13:35 quote the colon word for word (fetched). Douay-Rheims 'nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption'; Matos Soares 1932 'nem permitirás que o teu santo experimente corrupção'. Heard (draft 1): the blind reader took ‘ver a corrupção’ first as moral corruption, second as bodily decay. Kept: ‘vidére corruptiónem’ is the Latin’s and Acts’ (2:27, 13:35) image; the verse’s first colon (the soul, the dead) and 15:9 (the flesh) lean it toward the body for one who prays the whole.

options.label: deixareis o vosso santo ver
options.note: Ruling: 'deixar' + infinitive is Portuguese's 'let … see', the plain equivalent of the idiom (grammar, D2); 'ver' and 'corrupção' kept. 'deixar' is free, because derelínquere in the first colon is 'abandonar'.

options.label: permitireis que o vosso santo veja

forms.dabis: permitireis que o vosso santo veja

options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb (he has 'experimente' for 'ver'); a verb of permission named where the Latin has 'give'.

options.label: dareis ao vosso santo ver
options.note: The Latin's 'give' kept; Portuguese says 'dar a ver' only of showing something, so it is heard as a stiff calque.

decisions.why: delectátio: 'delight, pleasure' (Lewis & Short); τερπνότητες; only here (grep). The glossary keeps 'deleitoso' for delectáre (row jucúndus); delíciæ (138:11 in delíciis meis) is another word. in déxtera tua (ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ σου) → 'na vossa direita' — 'in', where 15:8 a dextris is 'à minha direita' (déxtera → a direita, glossary). The colon is verbless in the Latin, and stays so. Douay-Rheims 'at thy right hand are delights'; Matos Soares 1932 'na tua direita (encontram-se) delícias eternas'. Heard (draft 1): the blind reader listed ‘deleites’ as unknown. Kept; ‘delícias’ (delíciæ’s) is option 2.

options.label: deleites
options.note: Ruling: of delectáre's family (delectatio → deleite), keeping 'delícias' for delíciæ.

options.label: delícias
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the lovelier word, but delíciæ's; a proparoxytone.

decisions.why: The glossary row in finem (D27) says expressly: not usque in finem (15:11, 37:7). Here the Greek is εἰς τέλος. The clause is affirmative, so 'até o fim' carries none of the negation fault of 9:19. Douay-Rheims 'even to the end'; Matos Soares 1932 'eternas'.

options.label: até o fim
options.note: Ruling: 'usque in' → 'até', 'finem' → 'o fim': the Latin's words; the verse ends on the stressed 'fim'.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: The perpetuity the in finem row gives where it says 'for ever'; 'usque' is lost, and D27 keeps it apart.

choices.15:1: The psalm begins at 15:1 (the titulus Tituli inscríptio, ipsi David is out, D7). DO's 15:1 carries 15:2 after '‡' (second mediant); the inline '(2)' is not reproduced. speráre in → 'esperar em' (glossary), order as 7:2 'em vós esperei'. Deus meus es tu → 'Vós sois o meu Deus', as 117:28a (the same words also 21:11, 30:15, 139:7, 142:9 — grep). bonum (goods) → 'bens'.
choices.15:3: The verse is kept as loose as the Latin: the dative 'Aos santos' is taken up by 'neles' at the end. The Latin's 'meas' (my wills) against the Greek's αὐτοῦ (his) is followed (rule 1).
choices.15:4a: multiplicári → multiplicar-se (glossary); infírmitas → enfermidade (glossary row infírmus, which names 102:3 infirmitátes → enfermidades). eórum → 'deles', as open as the Latin (whose infirmities is not said).
choices.15:4b: memor esse → lembrar-se de (glossary). nómina → nomes. The last colon fronts ‘com os meus lábios’ so that the verse ends on ‘nomes’ (the stylist, rule 4).
choices.15:5: tu es, qui restítues → 'sois vós que me restituireis': the Latin turns from third person (Dóminus) to second (tu) within the verse, and so does the Portuguese. hereditátem meam mihi → 'me … a minha herança' (both kept). restitúere → restituir (34:17 restítue ánimam meam is the other place, grep).
choices.15:6: funes → cordas (glossary). étenim → pois (glossary). mihi twice → 'me … para mim'.
choices.15:7: benedícere + accusative → 'Bendirei o Senhor' (glossary). tríbuere … intelléctum → 'que me deu entendimento' (the glossary row bona tríbuere proposed exactly this for 15:7; intelléctus → entendimento).
choices.15:8: a dextris est mihi → 'está à minha direita' (as 90:7 'à tua direita'; no subject supplied — the Lord of the first colon is heard). ne commóvear → 'para eu não ser abalado', the build of 118:80 'para eu não ser envergonhado' (commovéri with movéri → ser abalado: one Greek verb, σαλεύω, as 14:5b). Before any critic read it, draft 1 had 'porque ele está à minha direita, para que eu não seja abalado' (+9 syllables on the Latin); shortened by the infinitive and by leaving the subject in the verb, as the Latin does. Draft 2: ‘antevia’ replaced by ‘via’ (the Latinist’s major; the stylist and the blind reader agreed).
choices.15:9: propter hoc → 'Por isso'; lætári / exsultáre → alegrar-se / exultar (glossary); ínsuper et → 'e ainda' (glossary, which wrote this colon); requiéscere → repousar (14:1); spes → esperança. = Acts 2:26 (fetched).
choices.15:10: The first colon's 'abandonar' (derelínquere, glossary) leaves 'deixar' free for the second colon's idiom. sanctum tuum → 'o vosso santo', lowercase (divine pronouns and titles lowercase; ὅσιος).
choices.15:11: Notas fecísti → 'Fizestes-me conhecer' (the formula for 76:15 Notam fecísti, 102:7 Notas fecit — grep). via → caminho. adimplére → encher (16:14b adimplétus est is the other place); 'vós' named so that the colon does not open on a clitic. lætítia → alegria (as 4:7 'destes alegria'). vultus → rosto (glossary). The verse = Acts 2:28 as far as 'vias vitæ' (Acts then reads 'replebis me jucunditate cum facie tua' — another Latin, fetched).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm15.txt, eleven prayed verses with DO's ids (15:1 — which carries 15:2 after '‡' — 3, 4a, 4b, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11). Collated against the Clementine Vulgate fetched from Bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-19-15.json): identical (hæreditas / hereditas is spelling). New Testament places fetched and read (Clementine, Bolls VULG): Acts 2:25–28 = 15:8–11a word for word (2:28b differs: 'replebis me jucunditate cum facie tua'), Acts 2:31 applies 15:10 to Christ, Acts 13:35 = 15:10b (consult/bolls-VULG-44-2.json, -44-13.json; ps013/show_vulg.py prints them).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps015.md. No Diurnal for this psalm. Sense from the Vulgate family (Douay-Rheims; Matos Soares 1932 by its text layer, his glosses and footnotes ignored). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Lewis & Short read for provideo, praeclarus, delectatio, conventiculum. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: Deus meus es tu (6 lines), conserváre (2), congreg- (17), sanguínibus (3), infírmitas (3), acceleráre (2), heréditas (24), præclárus (2), funes (3), intelléctum (8), a dextris (7), inférnus (21 lines), corrúptio (2), notas / notam fecísti (3), lætítia (14). Septuagintal readings kept against the Hebrew: 15:2 'não precisais dos meus bens', 15:3 the saints and 'fez maravilhosas as minhas vontades', 15:4a 'Multiplicaram-se as enfermidades deles', 15:4b 'ajuntamentos de sangue', 15:6 'excelentes', 15:7 'que me deu entendimento … os meus rins me repreenderam', 15:9 'a minha língua', 15:10 'corrupção', 15:11 'até o fim'. Decisions: 15. No vós imperative but 'Conservai-me' (safe).

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 15:1 last colon −3 (‘não precisais’ for ‘non eges’); 15:3 first colon +3 (the article and ‘estão’); 15:4b −4 / −3; 15:6 first colon +3 (‘lugares’ supplied for the neuter plural); 15:7 first colon −3; 15:8 second colon +5 (already shortened from +9 before any critic read it: ‘porque ele está à minha direita, para que eu não seja abalado’ → ‘porque está à minha direita, para eu não ser abalado’, the 118:80 build); 15:9 +3; 15:11 +3 / −4. No rhyme flag.

Draft 1. Two majors, nothing else; the marks confirmed. «A tradução conserva, nos demais versículos, o conteúdo e as imagens do latim, inclusive suas construções incomuns.» Passed in particular ‘Aos santos … fez maravilhosas’, ‘ajuntamentos’, ‘no inferno’, ‘deixareis o vosso santo ver a corrupção’, ‘deleites … até o fim’.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: ‘de sangue’ loses the plural of de sanguínibus → ‘de sangues’
outcomes.reason: Held against a major. The glossary row vir sánguinum → ‘homem de sangue’ (5:7b; 25:9, 54:24, 138:19) loses the same plural, and one ruling must serve every place of the plural (with 50:16 de sanguínibus); ‘sangues’ is heard in Portuguese as a slip or as kinds of blood. The blind reader heard both readings of the plural (bloodshed, blood rites) in ‘de sangue’. His fix is an option; an open glossary row asks Gustavo.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: ‘antevia’ brings in temporal foresight (Aulete) → ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’
outcomes.reason: The stylist and the blind reader (unknown word; ‘previa que veria’) agreed. His line exactly, in the Latin’s order.

audit.note: Draft 1. Five verses; best 15:10, worst 15:3. «O salmo tem sobriedade e, em boa parte, já encontra uma voz de oração em português … as imagens incomuns, por si mesmas, não precisam ser suavizadas.» Two taken (one in part), three refused with options.

outcomes.remark: the opening hangs; ‘fez maravilhosas’ sounds carried over from the Latin → ‘Quanto aos santos …, tornou maravilhosas’ (worst line)
outcomes.reason: The hanging dative is the Latin’s (taken up by in eis); ‘Quanto aos’ decides grammar the Latin leaves open. ‘tornou’ refused for the glossary’s mirificáre → ‘fazer maravilhoso’ (4:4); both kept as options (sanctis, mirificavit). The blind reader heard the Lord as subject, as meant.

outcomes.remark: ‘lábios’ at the verse’s end is a proparoxytone → ‘nem pelos meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’
outcomes.reason: His order taken (rule 4; D28); ‘com’ kept for per (the instrument), his ‘pelos’ an option.

outcomes.remark: ‘cálice’ at the mediant is a proparoxytone → ‘A parte da minha herança e do meu cálice é o Senhor’
outcomes.reason: The verse opens on Dóminus and turns to ‘sois vós’ — both colons open on the person; the proparoxytone accepted as at 90:1.

outcomes.remark: ‘e ainda até’ piles up particles; ‘ainda’ heard as duration → ‘e até a noite os meus rins também me repreenderam’
outcomes.reason: ínsuper et → ‘e ainda’ is the glossary’s, and 15:9 opens its last colon with the same words; ‘também’ breaks the pair. The slot widened so his line can be chosen.

outcomes.remark: ‘antevia’ suggests foreseeing the future → ‘Eu via sempre o Senhor diante de mim’
outcomes.reason: ‘via’ taken (with the Latinist); his ‘diante de mim’ refused — conspéctus keeps ‘vista’ (glossary, open) — and kept as an option.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 24 items, 3 unknown words (congregarei, antevia, deleites). Tests: ‘no inferno’ heard first as the place of punishment, second as the realm of the dead — the risk the inferno decision named; ‘ver a corrupção’ heard first as moral corruption; ‘antevia’ heard as foreseeing (fixed); ‘fez maravilhosas’ heard with the Lord as subject; ‘os meus rins’ heard as the organs (the renes row foresaw it).

outcomes.remark: ‘em vós esperei’: hoped in you (heard first) / waited for you
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; speráre holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘meus bens’: possessions (heard first) / the good I have or do
outcomes.reason: bona holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘na sua terra’: the saints’ (heard first) / the Lord’s / the speaker’s
outcomes.reason: ejus is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘fez maravilhosas’: the Lord (heard first) / someone unnamed
outcomes.reason: Heard as meant; the Latin names no subject.

outcomes.remark: ‘todas as minhas vontades neles’: relation unclear
outcomes.reason: So is the Latin; kept, not explained.

outcomes.remark: ‘as enfermidades deles’: the saints’ (heard first) / another group
outcomes.reason: eórum is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘depois se apressaram’: the people (heard first, purpose unclear) / the infirmities
outcomes.reason: The Latin says no more.

outcomes.remark: ‘os seus ajuntamentos’: those of the previous verse (heard first) / the Lord’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘ajuntamentos de sangue’: bloodshed (heard first) / blood rites / pools of blood
outcomes.reason: The first two are the two readings of de sanguínibus; evidence for holding the singular.

outcomes.remark: ‘dos seus nomes’: the people’s (heard first) / the gatherings’
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘me lembrarei … com os meus lábios’: to pronounce (heard first) / remember silently
outcomes.reason: Heard as meant (and still so in draft 2’s order).

outcomes.remark: ‘a parte da minha herança e do meu cálice’: my portion (heard first; the cup unclear)
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image; the cup is the psalter’s (10:7, 22:5).

outcomes.remark: ‘As cordas me caíram’: physical ropes (heard first) / measuring lines
outcomes.reason: funes → cordas (glossary); the image kept, not explained.

outcomes.remark: ‘até a noite’: until night (heard first) / even at night
outcomes.reason: usque ad noctem holds both; ‘até de noite’ is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘os meus rins me repreenderam’: the organs (heard first) / conscience
outcomes.reason: renes → rins (glossary, open): the organ named, as the row foresaw.

outcomes.remark: ‘antevia o Senhor’: foresaw (heard first) / saw before me
outcomes.reason: ‘via’ (with the Latinist and the stylist).

outcomes.remark: ‘não ser abalado’: physical / inner (heard first)
outcomes.reason: commovéri holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘a minha carne repousará’: body rests (heard first, possibly after death)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘a minha alma no inferno’: place of punishment (heard first) / realm of the dead
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s word (D22), as Acts 2:27, 31; the verse promises the soul is not left there. For Gustavo’s ear (glossary row inférnus).

outcomes.remark: ‘o vosso santo’: the speaker / another, possibly Jesus (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s ambiguity, and Acts 2:31’s reading.

outcomes.remark: ‘ver a corrupção’: moral corruption (heard first) / bodily decay
outcomes.reason: vidére corruptiónem is the Latin’s and Acts’ image; 15:9 (the flesh) and the first colon lean it to the body in prayer.

outcomes.remark: ‘com o vosso rosto’: the sight of it (heard first) / presence, favour
outcomes.reason: cum vultu tuo holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘na vossa direita’: the right hand (heard first) / the right side
outcomes.reason: in déxtera holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘até o fim’: end of the speaker’s life (heard first) / end of time
outcomes.reason: usque in finem holds both (D27: kept apart from in ætérnum).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: congregarei
outcomes.reason: congregáre’s own verb, one family with congregação.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: antevia
outcomes.reason: Replaced by ‘via’.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: deleites
outcomes.reason: delectátio’s word; ‘delícias’ is delíciæ’s (138:11) and option 2.

audit.note: v2. Two verses changed against draft 1: 15:8 ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’ (was ‘antevia’; the Latinist’s major, with the stylist and the blind reader); 15:4b ‘nem com os meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’ (the stylist’s order, rule 4). Slots widened so refused lines can be chosen: 15:5 (calicis, the whole first colon), 15:7 (noctem, with ‘e ainda’ and ‘os meus rins’), 15:4b (a ‘sangue’ slot under conventicula for the Latinist’s ‘de sangues’). HELD against the Latinist: 15:4b ‘de sangue’ (see the latinist step). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read). Script: ps015/revise_v2.py.
Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as draft 1 except 15:4b (−4 / −3, unchanged in count) and 15:8 first colon (13 against 15, no flag).

Draft 2 — the gate. One major, the same as draft 1’s and held on purpose: 15:4b ‘de sangue’ → ‘de sangues’. Nothing else; ‘Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista’ and ‘nem com os meus lábios me lembrarei dos seus nomes’ passed; the marks confirmed.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR (repeated): ‘de sangue’ loses the plural of de sanguínibus → ‘de sangues’
outcomes.reason: Held, as at draft 1: one ruling for the plural across the psalter (vir sánguinum → homem de sangue), and ‘sangues’ heard as a slip. Put to Gustavo as an open glossary row; the fix is selectable.
